source_title: Unlawful Use of an Unmanned Aircraft System
effective_date: 2018 (81 Del. Laws, c. 264), as amended through 84 Del. Laws, c. 514
uas_topic: Comprehensive UAS flight/privacy restriction, with FAA-authorization exemption and state preemption
regulated_activity: Flying a UAS over a mass gathering (1,500+ attendees), critical infrastructure, an active first-responder incident, or so as to harass or invade a person's privacy on private property or violate a protective order
requirement_type: Prohibition (misdemeanor, elevated if injury/damage occurs), with broad exemptions
summary: 11 Del. C. § 1334 makes it unlawful to knowingly operate, direct, or program a UAS to fly: over a sporting event, concert, race, festival, or other event with more than 1,500 people in attendance; over 'critical infrastructure' (petroleum refineries/storage, chemical storage/manufacturing, fuel storage, electric substations/power plants/generation facilities, military facilities, commercial port/harbor/rail-yard facilities, drinking-water treatment/storage facilities, correctional facilities, government buildings, and public safety buildings); over an incident where first responders are actively engaged; so as to harass a person on private property (cross-referencing § 1311(a)); so as to invade a person's privacy on private property (cross-referencing § 1335(a)(1),(2),(3),(4),(6)); or so as to violate a protective order. Four exemptions apply: law-enforcement use; flight over property with the owner/occupier's written permission; use by a higher-education institution for educational purposes in FAA compliance; and — notably broad — any UAS 'used for a commercial or other purpose if the operator is authorized by the Federal Aviation Administration.' Violation is an unclassified misdemeanor (first offense), a Class B misdemeanor (subsequent offense), or a Class A misdemeanor if physical injury or property damage results. Subsection (e) preempts all county/municipal authority to regulate UAS testing or operation; only the State may do so.

source_title: Special Use Permit Required for Drone/UAV Operation in Delaware State Parks
citation: 7 DE Admin. Code 9201, § 13.0 (Regulations Governing State Parks)
uas_topic: State park / public land UAS restriction
regulated_party: Any person, including AEC/commercial operators conducting infrastructure inspection, GIS, or similar government operational missions
regulated_activity: Operating a drone/UAV on or over DNREC Division of Parks and Recreation land or water
requirement_type: Prohibition except under an approved Special Use Permit
permit_or_approval_required: Yes — Special Use Permit; non-recreational (e.g., infrastructure inspection, GIS) uses additionally require a pre-approved FAA Part 107 exemption and issued FAA Certificate of Authorization (COA)
summary: DNREC's Division of Parks and Recreation requires a Special Use Permit for any drone/UAV operation on or over its land or water. Drones may not be flown around unprotected persons, in parking lots, near protected wildlife or active nesting/breeding areas, in Nature Preserves, within 100 ft of vulnerable property, or where the activity would be inconsistent with the park's character. To apply, the operator submits licensure, insurance, FAA documentation, and a flight plan to the park superintendent at least 10 days before the planned flight; a $75 administrative fee applies, plus a $35/hour supervision fee if park staff supervision is required. Required insurance coverage is $1,000,000 per occurrence / $3,000,000 aggregate, specifically covering drone use. For non-recreational uses — explicitly including 'government operational missions, such as infrastructure inspections, GIS, marketing, etc.' — the applicant additionally needs a pre-approved FAA Part 107 exemption and an issued FAA Certificate of Authorization (COA), plus Division of Parks and Recreation authorization.
